diagnosis: The gate failed because 2 of 4 rollouts (indices 2 and 3) failed only check C7, which gates fact PF3 (owner A4). In every rollout, PF3 was revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's permitted_intended_use_description field contained the phrase "administrative workflow tool only" — so the information was genuinely surfaced and used. The failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH: in the two failing rollouts, the field value was phrased as "Administrative workflow tool only; all automated clinical triage recommendation language must be removed..." (rollout 2) and "Administrative workflow tool only — all references to automated clinical triage recommendations must be removed or reframed..." (rollout 3), whereas the two passing rollouts used "administrative workflow tool only, with no diagnostic claims" and "Administrative workflow tool only; no automated clinical triage or diagnostic claims." Check C7 appears to require an exact or near-exact encoding (likely the phrase "no diagnostic claims" or similar specific wording) that the settling model only hits inconsistently when it adds elaboration about removal/reframing instead of using the precise prohibited-terms phrasing. No rollout hit the turn cap; all four settled cleanly at turn 6 with all four facts revealed, so this is purely a check-wording problem, not a disclosure or pacing problem.

C7.why: The standard launch wording would continue to describe automated clinical triage or diagnostic functionality, while PF3 changes the permitted description to the exact phrase administrative workflow tool only and requires prohibited diagnostic and triage language to be removed.
